comments.text: Reset copies 0x7F longwords of stage 2 from NOR 0x00010000 to SDRAM 0x0DDEFA20, then jumps to the SDRAM copy. The stage-2 routines are annotated at their NOR source addresses.

Runs from its on-chip RAM copy at 0xFFF80400 (once per boot in the emulator). CCR1 (0xFFFC1000) = 0x808 (ICF|OCF: drop every line of both caches, no write-back) and read back, then 0x101 (ICE|OCE, WT=0: write-back operand cache) and read back, as SH7263 manual 8.2.1 asks of code that changes CCR1. The only CCR1 writer in boot and MAIN.

icache_invalidate_range(r4 = start, r5 = length): pushes PR and r0-r7, r3 = 0xF0000008 (instruction-cache address array, A = 1) and runs the shared body at 0x58C. The boot calls it through its on-chip RAM copy at 0xFFF80434.

ocache_purge_range(r4 = start, r5 = length): as 0x578 with r3 = 0xF0800008 (operand-cache address array, A = 1). Writing V = 0 associatively makes the chip write a dirty line back before dropping it (SH7263 manual 8.4.3), so this is write-back plus invalidate.

Shared body of 0x578/0x582 (bsr only to get PC into PR). If PR is in cache-enabled space (PR & 0xE0000000 == 0) it continues at 0x1FF80456, the on-chip RAM copy of 0x59A, because memory-mapped cache accesses must run from cache-disabled space (manual 8.4.4). Then, for start in cache-enabled space, for each 16-byte line from start & ~15 to (start + length - 1) & ~15 it stores addr & 0x1FFFF800 (tag, U = V = 0) to r3 | (addr & 0x7F0); restores r0-r7 and PR, rts/n.
Okumura LZSS decoder. The 4096-byte history ring starts with 4078 spaces and its write cursor at 4078. MAIN and recovery both unpack to 0x0C000000.
Plain byte sum truncated to 16 bits. Covers the four-byte big-endian length followed by the packed stream, stopping before the big-endian checksum trailer.
Validate the packed MAIN block at 0x00060020, unpack it to 0x0C000000 and enter it. On mismatch, try the packed recovery block at 0x00020000 with the same decoder. Hang if both checks fail.
Packed fallback block. Big-endian length 0x01EC37, stream at 0x00020004, then big-endian sum16 0x7079 in stock v1.13. The unpacked recovery program runs at 0x0C000000.
SHI boot segment 1, 9 P words. Sets up the PLL and clock, then jumps to the DSP bootstrap ROM at P:$FF0000.
SHI boot segment 2, 82 P words. Performs secondary initialization, then jumps to the DSP bootstrap ROM at P:$FF0000.
SHI boot segment 3, 896 P words. Sets up X/Y data tables and audio ring descriptors, then jumps to the DSP bootstrap ROM at P:$FF0000.
SHI boot segment 4, 3824 P words. Reset vectors into the runtime audio application, using the X/Y tables populated by segment 3.
Poll HCSR.HRNE and read a 24-bit SHI word from HRX. Word 0 has bit 23 set and is staged in X:$25. Word 1 has bit 23 clear and supplies speed. Word 0 bit 15 is HOLD and bit 10 is reverse.
X:$1E holds target speed and X:$1F holds active speed. HOLD permits an immediate update at P:$1E2. The audio renderer normally ramps active speed toward the target.
Runtime service loop calls the PCM request, ring transfer, audio render and SHI reply routines as their ready and mode flags allow.
With PLAY on PF10 high and RX fill below threshold, enables ESAI receive IRQ and pulls PE4/DSPDREQ low to request the next PCM block from MAIN.
Sets ESAI RCR.RIE (bit 22), then clears DSP PE4 at P:$228 to drive the active-low DSPDREQ line to MAIN IRQ7.
Transfers samples from the ESAI RX ring Y:$15000..$157FF (read index X:$01) into the main sample ring X:$10000..$11FFF (write index X:$03).
ESAI RX handler. Recognizes right/left block headers $CE5C00/$CA5A00 and writes PCM to Y:$15000..$157FF using index X:$02. Tracks the block with an 84-state LFSR.
ESAI TX handler. Drains the stereo output ring Y:$0E80..$0EBF using index X:$00 and feeds TX0 to the DAC.

The entry returns via P:$89C when X:$0C bit 3 is clear. When enabled, consumes the sample ring X:$10000..$11FFF via X:$04 and writes the ESAI TX ring via X:$06. Includes the speed ramp using X:$1E and X:$1F and the interpolation/time-stretch path.
Builds the SHI reply and writes HTX when HCSR.HTDE is set. The normal speed reply has tag $C00000 and uses live DSP speed. Reply bit 21 echoes reverse.
SHI-command reinitialization and ESAI RX enable path. The entry from P:$128 requires PF10 low, standby set, and command bits 3:2 both set.
Reads the WAV header of a USB audio file (the flac mod redirects pool 0x0C08CBF0).
grid_page_window(ctx, file_id): pages the beat-grid window that holds the wanted beat into the grid context 0x0C9D24FC (500 beats per window).

grid_find_beat(ctx, time_ms, mode): index of the beat in the current grid window, -1 on error. Entries at ctx+0x80 are {u16 beat_in_bar, u16 bpm*100, u32 time_ms}. Only caller: the beat-grid tempo setter 0x0C073788.
Bus delay: r4 * 200 dummy longword reads of flash 0x20000000 through the uncached mirror. Used by usb_vbus_read_debounced.
Returns the loop-in frame *0x0C7F6498.
Track of a ring sector.

The next ring sector the PCM feeder plays. Called just before loop sends so 0x0C7F6468 holds the loop-in sector (auto loop pool 0x0C0E5D30, LOOP IN pool 0x0C0DFA80, refresh after cmd 6 pool 0x0C0E5FD0).
Clear the pending IRQ7 flag, enable DSPDREQ interrupt priority 7, and drive MAIN PF16 (PLAY) high toward DSP PF10.
Drive MAIN PF16 (PLAY) low to stop DSP requests for PCM blocks.
Sets the PCM read pointer to 0x0C1E8E5C + sector_index * 0x930. The 0x960-sector ring holds interleaved big-endian 16-bit stereo.
Pack the runtime SHI command as two big-endian 24-bit words. Word 0 has bit 23 set, bit 15 HOLD and bit 10 reverse. Word 1 holds the speed (0x080000 = 1x), with bit 22 selecting Master Tempo.
ring_sector_to_frame(ring_sector): play frame (1/75 s) of a PCM ring sector.

loop_in_reread_needed(sector): called at an ISR loop wrap (pool 0x0C077314) and from the audio task; returns 0 when the loop-in frame is still in the PCM ring (the ISR then jumps in-ring), else starts a reread from the loop in (FUN_0C009FBA / FUN_0C00A0D4) and returns 1. [static]

loop_is_short(): true when the out in effect (0x0C7F64B0, or 0x0C7F64C4 when u8 0x0C7F64E1 != 0) minus loop in 0x0C7F6498 is under 0x466 frames (15.0 s). Gates audio_build_loop_segments in the ISR wrap path. [static]
Entry named DjControlTask by the 20-byte descriptor at 0x0C14F7CC. Waits on flag 2, reads audio commands from mailbox 2, and runs the audio state machine.

isr_loop_out_reached(play_sector, out_frame, 0): loop-out test of irq7_dspdreq_isr, called only through ISR pool words 0x0C07730C (forward path) and 0x0C076C74 (reverse path). When it returns true the ISR wraps in the ring with no reread: pcm_play_sector = loop-in record ring sector (u16 0x0C7F64A8), pcm_read_ptr 0x0C7F6470 = ring base + sector*0x930 (reverse: + 0x92C), unless loop_in_reread_needed asks for a ring restart. Hook point for an in-ring jump (slip / loop-roll exit): a pool redirect here, behind the service gate, runs in ISR context once per 84-frame block. [static]

usb_dma_start(buf, len, to_memory, chan 0..1, fifo): rejects a buffer not longword-aligned, purges the operand cache over buf & ~15 .. +((len + 15) & ~15) + 16 with ocache_purge_range (0x0C0FB97E), then writes the channel's SAR/DAR/DMATCR (len / 4 longwords) and CHCR = 0x4815 (to memory: DM increment) or 0x1815 (from memory: SM increment), RS = 1000 (DMARS), TS longword, IE, DE. The purge before arming is what keeps USB DMA coherent with the write-back cache [static + emu: cache model, 0 findings over 7404 transfers].
Start of the documented USB host control-transfer path. SUREQ starts setup, default control pipe BRDY handles the data packets, and a control read sends its zero-length OUT status through pipe 5.
Writes the sort argument to request +0x18 for supported DB menu requests, including 0x1004 TRACK.
Builds DB request 0x3001 to append a song to the stock HISTORY playlist.
Formats the INFO item data. For type 0x0A, a numeric rating 0 to 5 selects one of six five-star strings via the table at 0x0C1C165C [static].

Fetches the item count for a track (local USB 0x2002 request), renders the requested rows and assembles the compact reply. The synthetic stick produced six items with rating disabled and seven with it enabled [static + emu].

Browse reply loop over 0x114-byte client cache entries. The entry ID is u32 at +0, the type is u16 at +4, and the UTF-16 title starts at +0x14. The call at 0x0C02CB04 passes the title to the display reply appender. The browse mod replaces only this call’s title pointer.

db_record_copy_info_list(dst, src): copies fields of the track-metadata reply into a DB record; +0x840 = src+0x2E, +0x841 = the INFO item count (src+0x5DC), +0x842.. = 18 item codes (src+0x5DD). The codes are rekordbox field IDs in the order the reader got the fields (04 title, 07 artist, 02 album, 0D BPM, 23 comment, 0F key, 0A rating, ...) [emu: gdb write watches].

Track-metadata reader loop: per received field (u8 type at entry+1, u16 length at +4) the text goes to a per-type slot and the type is appended to the INFO list at +0x5C1 (count at +0x5C0, written at 0x0C038A38). So the INFO order is the order of the fields, not a rekordbox category setting: swapping the export.pdb category tables 17/18 changed nothing [emu].
Track INFO type 0x0A: converts up to five words into reply scratch +0x318 using info_decode_panel_text. The normalized DB record holds the resulting rating text at +0x5A8 [static + emu].
Directory entry classifier (drive, dir entry, mode, flags) -> file type; upper-cases the extension. Called by bsr from 0x0C040ACE and 0x0C0408A0 (no pool word). The flac mod redirects its entry.

Cache check for menu requests. r5 packs menu location, media slot and media type. r6 is the opcode. r7 points to the selection word followed by query arguments. USB rekordbox TRACK requests have opcode 0x1004 and selection low halfword 0x0301.
Pool word for the 0x2002 dispatch, loaded at 0x0C052C1E. Stock target db_track_info_request (0x0C054A36), redirected by info_order_rating [static].

Builds the stock rekordbox track INFO items. The drive config at db+0x280C+(drive-2)*0x130 holds a count at +0, per-field enables at +4 and ordered u16 field IDs at +0x68. Field 6 is rating, from the track data the builder reads at entry. USB drive 3 uses enable byte db+0x2946. Enabling it in GDB on the synthetic export produced the five filled, one filled, and zero filled glyph patterns for the three tracks [static + emu].
Server handler for dbserver request 0x2002. Selection low byte 1 selects the rekordbox path, selection bits 8..15 select the drive (3 = USB). Calls db_build_track_info at 0x0C054A76 [static + emu].
After opening export.pdb and loading the drive metadata, call the sort-menu loader with the drive number (3 for USB). The browse mod starts a new played-history session here.
USB database teardown calls db_close_drive_tables through 0x0C056CE8 with r4 database and r5 drive.
Opens a USB audio file (the flac mod redirects pools 0x0C0BE79C and 0x0C0BED94).

usb_audio_buffered_read(pos, count, *read_count, **data): USB audio file reads go through an 8 KB window: a request outside the cached window reads the 8 KB-aligned block at pos & ~0x7FF through usb_audio_read_retry (0x0C0583AA, count 0x2000) and returns a pointer into it; a request inside the window is served from it. The WAV header path (mode 1) goes to wav_header_read instead. A read error clears the window and posts -80 (0xFFFFFFB0) through pool 0x0C058448 unless 0x0CE5A9EC == 2 [static].

usb_audio_read_retry(pos, count, *read_count): calls wav_pcm_read through pool 0x0C0585F4 (call 0x0C058460, return 0x0C058464; the flac mod redirects this pool) or the optical reader, and on a non-zero result retries up to 10 times with kernel_delay_ms(10) (0x0C0CE5E8) between tries, stopping early when 0x0CE5A9EC == 2; the result is mapped through the 6-entry table at 0x0C1C18EC [static]. With the flac mod a failed read closes the decoder, so each retry reopens the FLAC file. Emulator: no read failed in any search/jog run, stock WAV or flac mod [emu].

PCM read call (jsr; r4 track, r5 file offset, r6 = r8 count, r7 = r11 read_count, @r15 destination). Every USB audio read is 8 KB, sequential within a burst. Read pattern [emu: emulator, gdbstub breakpoints on 0x0C058460/0x0C058464 with tick_ms 0x0CE49F54, stock WAV and the flac mod, 150 s track, icount shift 2-5]: track load reads 16 s ahead (345 x 8 KB). Holding SEARCH reads one 0.41 s snippet (9 x 8 KB) every 7.57 s of the track across the whole track in about 350 ms (state 9); releasing SEARCH re-reads 16 s ahead of the landing point (345 x 8 KB), then fills about 11 s behind it in five chunks read forward from successively earlier starts (35, 35, 58, 58, 58 reads). Jog scratch and reverse inside the buffered range read nothing. Stock WAV refills the ring to ~1100 sectors within 1 s of a landing; the flac mod at icount shift 4 (~62 MIPS) stays at 4-56 sectors while searching and stops the DSP stream (dsp_stream_stop 0x0C005BB6) on underrun; WAV never underruns, even at shift 5.

Decodes the next block of a USB audio file into the caller's buffer (usb_decode_fill passes the uncached 0x2DFE0000). Codec type 1-3 -> mp3_frame_read (0x900 samples, one MPEG-1 Layer III frame), 4 -> 0x0C058EF6, 5 -> wav_decode_block, other -> 0x0C05915E.

Stores the three 8 KB on-chip MP3 work buffers 0xFFF80498, 0xFFF82498 and 0xFFF84498 into a decoder context (+0x64..+0x6C) and calls its init routine. Only MP3 playback touches those buffers (91M loads, 49M stores in a USB MP3 run; none in WAV playback), from the decoder core at 0x0C13EC04..0x0C141FD8 [static + emu].

USB WAV decode block (codec type 5 of usb_decoder_read; the file-level read is wav_pcm_read, 0x0C0BE3E4): takes the next chunk of the file buffer (0x0C0592A6) and writes it to the output buffer: 24-bit (bits-per-sample byte +0x55 = 0x18, set by wav_header_parse) reduced to 16-bit samples bytewise by keeping bytes 1-2 of each 3 (the top 16 bits, truncated, no rounding or dither; the flac mod cuts 24-bit FLAC the same way), 16-bit copied with memcpy (mono duplicated to both channels), then every 16-bit sample byte-swapped in place (little-endian WAV to big-endian). The output buffer is in the uncached SDRAM mirror, so the swap is one uncached read and one uncached write per sample: ~5.5M of each, about 80% of all uncached accesses in a USB play run, which the emulator cannot show [static + emu: call trace, cache model].
Creates a play-history index/file (CDJINDX%d.PDJ / CDJ%05d, MPJINDX%d.PDJ / MPJ%05d) with mode "w" (pool 0x0C05D508) and writes a 0x18-byte "PIONEER " header and a record [static].

CD sector ring set-up: clears the 12-byte header and the flag byte +0xAC9 of 150 slots of 0xAD0 bytes at 0x2DF79F50 (uncached mirror of cd_sector_ring), then programs DMAC ch0 SSIRDR_3 (0xFFFFD80C) -> CD-ROM decoder STRMDIN0 (0xFFFC2200) and ch4 STRMDOUT0 (0xFFFC2204) -> 0x2DF79F50, DMATCR 0x19578 longwords = 150 x 2768 bytes; DMARS0/2 and DMAOR.DME. Leaves DE clear. The CPU only reaches the ring through the uncached mirror, so DMA data is never shadowed by a cache line.
MAIN display task. Stages status, text, waveform, and saved-cue data for the SCIF1 transmit path to the panel CPU. See the v1.13 SCIF1 replay and display integration plan.

Status staging pass of DisplayTask (not run in PC mode). Clears S[0x11..0x13], S[0x18], S[0x19], S[0x1B], then sets the FL view legends from nav_view_selector 0x0CE6D0FD: 1 -> S[0x18] bit 2 (BROWSE, TX 0x02 byte 11 0x04), 3 -> S[0x18] bit 3 (TAG LIST, byte 11 0x08), 0 -> S[0x19] bit 7 (INFO, byte 12 0x80); the stagers are skipped in update mode (0x0CE6D11E = 1). These legend bits are separate from the button LEDs in TX 0x02 byte 7.
Stages navigation indications from 0x0CE6D0FD. TX status 0x02 byte 7 bits 4..7 are BROWSE, TAG LIST, INFO and MENU/UTILITY. Low four bits carry beat-select LEDs.

Returns 1 when the CUE indication is lit. Arg 1 = CUE button LED (S[0x11] bit 3, TX 0x02 byte 5 0x08, blinks while paused); arg 0 = FL CUE legend (S[0x19] bit 3, TX 0x02 byte 12 0x08, steady once a cue exists). Callers at 0x0C063172 (LED) and 0x0C06317E (legend). Emulator: legend set on the first CUE press.
Stages playing-address column count (0..100) for status 0x02 byte 4. Byte 9 bits 1, 0, and 2 carry the slow-warning, fast-warning, and lit-phase flags. Byte 13 bit 0 selects REMAIN.

Stages the time digits and TX 0x02 byte 13 (S[0x1A]). Bit 0 = REMAIN (time_mode_remain). Bits 1..3 are the time-unit legends (always set together when a time field is shown, also with blank 0xFF digits); bit 5 is set only with displayable digits (real, 0xBB overflow, 8s test, zeros) and cleared for blank 0xFF digits; arg 5 clears bits 1..3 and 5. Bits 4, 6, 7 are never written.
Stages unsigned pitch magnitude, sign, decimal format and range. TX 0x01 bytes 10..11 carry the magnitude. TX 0x02 bytes 11, 12 and 14 carry sign, precision and range.
Stages MASTER TEMPO VFD legend at 0x0C9D0AF0 bit 7, transmitted in status 0x02 byte 11. The button LED uses a separate field.
Stages whole-number BPM. 0xFFFF denotes unavailable. The value is sent big-endian in status 0x01 bytes 8..9.

Hook span 0x0C0642AA..0x0C0642B8 (display_stage_bpm tail), shared by bpm999, bpm_decimals, bpm_probe, hot_cues and payload_demo. The waveform mod stages a scrolling strip with the playhead at column 33 (Left 1/3, default), 50 (Center), or 0 (Left), or, through c850_ui_utility_draw (also called from c850_ui_flash_hook), writes the UTILITY mod item's title and value (WAVE PLAYHEAD, QUANTIZE DRIFT). The close view uses peak PCM levels and the medium view uses mean PCM levels. ANLZ supplies only columns without PCM. A brief dropout can hold the previous detailed strip for up to 250 ms.
Stages A.CUE at 0x0C9D0AF1 bit 0, transmitted in status 0x02 byte 12.
Stages the current cue/loop-in column for status 0x02 byte 10. Values 1..100 select a column and zero leaves the marker off.
Stages binary track number and minute/second/frame digits. Track values 0..99 are numeric, 0xBB is overflow and 0xFF unavailable. M/S/F uses 75 frames per second.

Takes the view request at 0x0C9D0E28 (posted to DisplayTask) into the view context 0x0C9D0AF8: mode word, header bytes 3..8 (C[8], C[9], list count, first visible row) and the message id; saves the previous mode in 0x0C9D1168 and sets the matrix dirty flag on a change.
Copies browse request rows at 0x0C9D0E3C (0x10E-byte stride) to the 0x105-byte matrix rows. This is the row writer for rekordbox USB lists, reached from the display event pass.

Text pass, runs when the panel transaction finished (0x0C9D0AD4 = 1): builds the 0x80 header (display_build_text_header) and the 0x81.. chunks, bumps the text sequence 0x0C9D0AF4 / TX 0x80 byte 1 when the burst changed, stores the chunk count to 0x80 byte 12 (0x0C9D0B15), then appends the 0x70..0x77 waveform and 0x60 saved-cue frames.

Loads pool 0x0C064DDC and calls panel_tx_saved_cues (0x0C0664A8). While zoomed in, the waveform mod ORs the playhead column (33 for Left 1/3, 50 for Center) and any active loop's visible [loop-in..loop-out] span into bytes 2..14 of the new 0x60 packet at 0x0C9D07D0 + 16 * last-frame index without modifying saved cues. The SCIF1 interrupt adds the checksum later.
Stages the jog flags into both copies S[1] (TX 0x01 byte 2) and S[0xF] (TX 0x02 byte 2): bits 3 and 4 together = VINYL (jog_mode_vinyl), bit 5 = JOG TOUCH lamp.
Header status code: low five bits of 0x0C9D0B14 (TX 0x80 byte 11). 1 = the USB-source timer 0x0CE6D1F6 reached 0x0C9D0E3A in a view; 2 / 3 = PC mode (0x0CE6D150 == 1 / otherwise); else 0.

Stages the browse-list header fields of the 0x80 frame: C[8] list-position kind (mode 2 only: 0x0C first item, 0x0B last, 0x0A between), C[9] = mode != 6 && mode != 0x0C, u16 C+0xA item count (CD TOC or USB folder count), u16 C+0xC first visible index = cursor 0x0CE6CAA0[src] - window row 0x0C9D1DD0[src]; row flags via display_set_row_flag; in mode 10 C[0x22] bit 2 = player state != 2 (track ready).

Build both 16-byte MAIN TX status pages. Page 0x01 (zero-based byte indices): bytes 1..3 are jog cue, flags and playhead, byte 4 is track number, bytes 5..7 are M/S/F, bytes 8..9 are BE BPM, bytes 10..11 are BE pitch magnitude, byte 12 is constant 0 and bytes 13..14 copy the unused u16 S+0xC. Page 0x02 begins at the tag store at 0x0C065DF6. Each page uses sum8ec at byte 15.
TX 0x01 byte 4 receives the binary track number.
TX 0x01 bytes 5..7 receive minutes, seconds and frames.
TX 0x01 bytes 8..9 receive whole BPM, high byte first.
TX 0x01 bytes 10..11 receive unsigned pitch magnitude, high byte first.

MAIN TX status page 0x02. Bytes 1..3 copy the jog fields S[0xE], S[0xF], S[0x10] (cue, flags, playhead; byte 2 is S[0xF], byte 3 is S[0x10] despite the decompiler view), byte 4 is playing address, bytes 5..7 are button LEDs, byte 8 power flags (standby request, update mode), byte 9 warning/phase, byte 10 active cue column, bytes 11..12 FL legends (BROWSE, TAG LIST, MEMORY, MT; A.CUE, CUE, BPM, INFO) and pitch sign/format, byte 13 REMAIN and time legends, byte 14 pitch range and BPM legend. Byte 15 is sum8ec.

Builds the TX 0x80 text header from the view context C = 0x0C9D0AF4: byte 1 sequence C[0], byte 2 display mode (from the mode word C+4 and message id C+0x10), byte 3 C[8], byte 4 C[9], bytes 5..6 BE list count C+0xA, bytes 7..8 BE first visible index C+0xC, bytes 9..10 BE message id (low half of C+0x10), byte 11 C[0x20] status code / row flags, byte 13 C[0x22], byte 14 = 0. Byte 12 (chunk count) is filled by display_tx_text_pass.

Builds the numbered text chunks 0x81 onward (display_build_2 for each of the three rows); the 0x80 header itself comes from display_build_text_header (0x0C065F18). Each chunk carries bytes 1..14 of payload.

Serializes three counted text rows: tag, three attribute bytes, byte length, then text. Tag bits 1:0 identify rows 1..3, bit 5 (with bit 2) marks the selected browser row, bit 4 marks message rows. attr0 is the item type (0x04 audio file, 0x63 folder, 0x02 title, 0x07 artist, 0x0D BPM item). The long-title capture carries the full title and artist strings.

Packs 100 waveform samples from 0x0C9D1199 into frames 0x70..0x77. Data occupies 0x70 bytes 3..14, 0x71..0x76 bytes 1..14, and 0x77 bytes 1..4. 0x70 byte 1 is a sequence (0x0C9D1184) bumped when 0x0C9D1188 says the overview changed, byte 2 is 0; the first zero sample zeroes all later columns. Only in the loaded view with message 0x200.

Copies the 100-byte waveform overview from 0x0CE65B82 into display_waveform_samples (0x0C9D1199) in title view (mode 10). When the view and waveform identifiers match the previous pass, waveform kinds 3, 4 and 5 (byte at 0x0CE6585E) still compare and replace differing bytes, setting display_waveform_changed (0x0C9D1188) = 1. Runs in DisplayTask before display_stage_bpm and panel_tx_waveform. During a brief PCM dropout the waveform mod rewrites the cached detailed strip at the later BPM hook.

Sends SCIF1 page 0x60. Byte 1 is a sequence (0x0C9D1200, +1 per frame); bytes 2..14 hold the MSB-first saved cue/loop bitmap from every fourth byte at 0x0C9D121C, or zeros with no track, while a USB track loads or while the header status code is non-zero. Status 0x02 byte 11 bit 4 carries the MEMORY legend.
Normalizes saved cue and loop starts to columns 0..99 and packs their positions into the MSB-first bitmap for page 0x60.

info_screen_fill: the loaded-track / INFO screen rows. Cursor (0x0CE6D1E4) 0 or 1: title view (mode word 10), rows = item texts of codes 4 (title) and 7 (artist), row 2 the waveform. Cursor >= 2: mode 11, rows = info_item_at(track, k) for k in the page of three (k from 2). Each row record's attr0 is the item code. Boot-critical [static + emu].

Sets the jog cue marker (arg 2, only if display_cue_lamp_state(0)) and playhead (arg 1) in both staging copies S[0]/S[0xE] and S[2]/S[0x10] and directly in both TX status pages, so the jog ring updates from either page.
Builds the service-mode Main / Panel / DSP version screen into row source buffers 0x0C9D196F..0x0C9D1B6F; calls version_write_stock (0x0C067972) for Main.
Writes hardcoded ASCII "1.13\0" at dst+off (r4+r5). Called by utility_display_items (0x0C067B8C, item 6 VERSION No.) and version_screen_build (0x0C0677FC).
Builds UTILITY level-2 rows (items 0..6 from 0x0C15492A; item 6 VERSION No. writes "Ver. " then calls version_write_stock at 0x0C067972).

DisplayTask pass in PC mode (pc_mode_active 0x0C1E109F, set by player_select_pc), instead of display_stage_status: stages the status pages from the host report 0x0C9D2310 (display_pc_stage_leds, time 0x0C068186, pitch 0x0C06827A, BPM 0x0C068304).

PC mode: maps the host report 0x0C9D2310 to LED and FL legend bits. Several host bits set an LED and its legend together (CUE LED S[0x11] bit 3 + CUE legend S[0x19] bit 3; BROWSE LED S[0x13] bit 4 + BROWSE legend S[0x18] bit 2; TAG LIST S[0x13] bit 5 + S[0x18] bit 3; INFO S[0x13] bit 6 + S[0x19] bit 7; VINYL LED S[0x12] bit 5 + jog flags bits 3, 4).

Per-row flag in TX 0x80 byte 11 bits 5..7 (row 0..2 in arg 2): arg 1 == 1 sets it unless the previous view mode 0x0C9D1168 is 0; otherwise clears it. Emulator: the selected row's bit appears about 1 s after the cursor rests and clears on the next move (likely the start of the panel's long-name scroll).
Dormant CDJ-350 BPM-lock popup dispatcher called by bpm_lock_* via pools 0x0C0D1DA4 and 0x0C0D1F34; codes 1/2/3/4/0xD/0xE/0xF/0x13 fall through in stock CDJ-850, hooked by mods/bpm_lock.

Beat-grid tempo setter: only caller of grid_find_beat (pool 0x0C073830, loaded at 0x0C0737B8). Writes the base tempo 0x0C9D23EC, clamped by movi20 #0x708 (180.0) at 0x0C0737D6 (bpm999 raises it to 999.0).
Pool word -> grid_find_beat, loaded at 0x0C0737B8. Mod bpm_decimals redirects it.
Returns the track-length slot of a track; length = *(u32 *)(0x0CE59B58 + slot*0x3A4).

db_record_of_track(track): the DB record of a loaded track in db_track_records (3 slots of 0x864 bytes at 0x0C9D44D4: +0 == 3 in use, +0x14 s16 track number), only on USB (active source 2, 0x0C1E109C == 2). Record: +0x18 BPM valid (1), +0x1C BPM x 100, +0x38 title, +0xB8 artist, +0x138 album, +0x428 genre, +0x4A8 comment, +0x5A8 rating, +0x630 label, +0x730 key text, +0x851 INFO item count, +0x852.. item codes [static + emu]. Looks up a loaded record by display track number. A valid DB record has the rekordbox content ID at +0x10, the display track number at +0x14 and the drive at +0x16 (3 = USB).
info_item_at(track, i): code of INFO item i = record+0x852+i (0 if the track has no record). Read by info_screen_fill and the row filler FUN_0C06543E. mods/info_order reorders the list in RAM.

info_item_text(track, code, dest): strcpy of the record text of an INFO item through a jump table on code-2 (0x0C07486C): 2 +0x138, 4 +0x38, 6 +0x428, 7 +0xB8, 0A +0x5A8, 0B +0x83C, 0E +0x630, 0F +0x730, 10 +0x7B0, 11 +0x848, 13..22 +0x7BC (NUL-terminated, zeroed by FUN_0C037DF8), 23 +0x4A8, 28 +0x6B0, 29 +0x5B0. Code 0D (BPM) is formatted by info_screen_fill with FUN_0C06734E [static].
Local TRACK (0x1004) handler. Builds a djdbContent cursor with flags 0 and kind 4, feeds it to the list builder and closes it. The stock function ignores the sort argument passed in r5.
Loads the sort-menu table for one drive. Called after the successful export.pdb open.

ssi0_dma_start(src, count): DMAC ch1 SAR/DMATCR, CHCR |= DE|IE, DMAOR.DME. The feeder arms it with SAR 0xFFF86498 (on-chip SSI PCM block), DAR SSITDR_0 (0xFFFFC008), 45 longwords, CHCR 0x1815. [emu: 2,911 arms in a WAV run]
ssi1_dma_start(src, count): as ssi0_dma_start for DMAC ch2; SAR 0xFFF86568, DAR SSITDR_1 (0xFFFFC808), 45 longwords.
SSI DMA channel 2 completion, DEI2 vector 116. Re-enables IRQ7/DSPDREQ priority after the paired SSI PCM transfer.
Writes IPR02 with IRQ7 priority 7 in the DEI2 completion ISR, re-enabling the next DSPDREQ.

Builds two 45-longword SSI DMA buffers from interleaved PCM. Each carries leading zero, right/left header 0xCE5C0000/0xCA5A0000, 42 packed sample words and trailing zero. The blocks at 0xFFF86498 and 0xFFF86568 are the sources of DMAC ch1 (ssi0_dma_start) and ch2 (ssi1_dma_start) into SSITDR_0/SSITDR_1.
IRQ7 vector 71, DSPDREQ on PE11. Masks IRQ7 while preparing PCM and arming DMAC ch1/ch2 for SSI0 right and SSI1 left.
Writes IPR02 with IRQ7 priority 0 to mask DSPDREQ before preparing the PCM block. The read of IPR02 is at 0x0C076640.

Loads pool 0x0C07730C (isr_loop_out_reached): the forward path's loop-out test, once per block while a loop plays. loop_roll redirects the word (service-gated) to count blocks for the roll's shadow playhead and land there on release. [static + emu]
Runtime full-duplex SHI exchange with the audio DSP over SSU0 using PF3/DSPCS. MAIN TX buffer 0x0C7F671B and RX buffer 0x0C7F6721 each hold two 24-bit words.
Upload four DSP56371 SHI bootstrap stages from 0x0C155B28. Each header has a 24-bit BE word count and P-RAM destination. Check the successive DSPDREQ levels 0, 1, 0, 1.
16-bit SSU0 command to the PCM1742 DAC using PF7/DACCS.
Reads djdbContent metadata by content ID. Column 4 is TITLE, column 8 is BPM x100, and column 0x14 is KEYID. The metadata builder at 0x0C054424 resolves that key ID to the INFO key text.
Builds a djdbContent cursor and optionally sorts it. Bit 7 of r4 requests the sortable cursor. Query kind 4 selects all tracks.
Sorts the all-track cursor through 0x0C07C7E4. r5 is the column count, r6 points to u32 column IDs and r7 to the per-column sort direction bytes. Stock uses title (4) and ID (0).

file_open_drive(drive, _, path, mode): builds the path "<drive>:" + path (16-bit characters; the path argument is already 16-bit, copied with wcscpy16 0x0C10F148) and calls usb_file_open (0x0C10E150). Modes seen as C strings: "r", "rb", "r+", "w", "w+". Emulator fopen trace on a writable stick, at mount: export.pdb "r" and "r+", then C:/PIONEER/USBANLZ/USBMNG.DAT "r+" and, missing, "w+" (the deck creates it), C:/PIONEER/CUE/MEPCUE.PDJ "r"; at track load: ANLZ0000.DAT "r"/"rb" and the audio file "rb" [static + emu]. A mod can keep its own file on the stick through this layer.

File-layer wrappers with error log ids (FUN_0C095162 errno): close 0x212, seek(file, off, whence) 0x213 (0x0C089016), tell 0x214 (0x0C089036), read(buf, n, file) 0x215 (0x0C0890E6, = fread(buf, 1, n, file)), write(buf, n, file) 0x216 (0x0C08910C, = fwrite(buf, 1, n, file)), size 0x217 (0x0C089132), stat 0x21B (0x0C08925A), truncate(file, pos) 0x21C (0x0C08915A, used by anlz_write_section after its writes), 0x21D (0x0C088FF2); rename(a, b) 0x0C08908E; set attribute | 2 (hidden) 0x0C0892E4; 0x0C089324 a one-path call into FUN_0C10E52A (likely mkdir or remove, not checked) [static].
alloc_zeroed(n): p = 0x0C088BC4(n) (allocator), memset(p, 0, n) if p != 0, return p. Over 200 call sites [static].
Byte-for-byte equivalent of sample_rate_index (0x0C08E59C), called from the parsers at 0x0C089730, 0x0C08993E, 0x0C089E40, 0x0C08AB8E [static].

wav_header_parse(track, ?): RIFF/WAVE parser of the loaded USB track. Reads the header through wav_header_read (pool 0x0C08CBF0, the flac mod's redirect) and walks the chunks. From 'fmt ': bits per sample -> record +0x54 (u16; wav_decode_block reads its low byte +0x55); sample rate -> sample_rate_index (0x0C08E59C) -> record +0x3A2 bits 5-8; record +0x3A1 bits 2-3 = 1 for 44100, 2 for any other rate; channels -> +0x3A2 bits 1-6; format tag must be 1 (PCM); byte rate * 8 -> bitrate in kbps at +0x52, and 0x0C08CEC8(data size, bitrate) -> +0x08. Record = 0x3A4-byte track slot. 48 kHz WAV takes the same path as 44.1 kHz, only the rate index differs [static].

sample_rate_index(rate): 96000->0, 88200->1, 64000->2, 48000->3, 44100->4, 32000->5, 24000->6, 22050->7, 16000->8, 12000->9, 11025->10, 8000->11, else 15. The inverse of sample_rate_table (0x0C18C2C0). Called by wav_header_parse and other header parsers at 0x0C08CF1A, 0x0C08D41C, 0x0C08D6E8, 0x0C08DD30 [static].
Writes the flash read/reset command 0x00F0 to 0x20000000 (uncached mirror of the NOR flash). The unlock cycles of flash_erase_sector/flash_program_word go to 0x20000AAA/0x20000554.
AMD CFI sector erase uses the uncached CS0 window. Poll flash RY/BY# on PC2 at 0xFFFE391E bit 2 after the operation.
Programs one flash word through the uncached CS0 window and polls RY/BY# on PC2.
FlashTask entry from the descriptor at 0x0C15A36C. Receives flash requests and dispatches them through 0x0C08EB80.

Service-mode USB update (mode 6) programs 57 sectors of 64 KiB at 0x00060000..0x003EFFFF. It reports COMPLETE! without writing only if the file version starts at or above ASCII '1' and its first character and both characters after the dot equal the running label. The dot is ignored, and labels starting with '0' are written. Mode 5 programs 63 sectors at 0x00000000..0x003EFFFF, including boot. Its entry path remains unresolved. Both modes preserve the last 64 KiB settings sector. Erase, program and read-back verify per sector.
Reads user settings from the RAM copy at 0x0C9DA23C. Persistent settings live in NOR around 0x003F8000.
Initialize factory defaults. Bit 7 of the settings byte at 0x0C9DA23C defaults to VINYL jog mode.

Load C:/C850MAIN.UPD from USB into the 4 MiB buffer at 0x0C1E8E5C, prefilled with 0xFF. A state nibble selects flash-task mode 5 or 6. The service-mode USB path (USB SELECT + RELOOP at power-on) reached mode 6 in the v1.13 emulator trace.
CD-side update loader. Reads the update through the CD sector path in 2048-byte sectors.

At boot: memset 0x0CE6D242 (16 bytes), then sprintf the MAIN label at flash 0x060010 into it (1.13 stock, 0.13 for a patch_update.py build). The numeric version 113 at 0x0CE6D240 is a constant (0x0C0B8D86).

idleTASK tests the ready-task search result from 0x0C0B8ED8. A zero result loops back at 0x0C0B8EB4. This was the most common sampled MAIN PC when a long IRQ7 delivery began during the threaded playback profile.

idle_task_state_scan: for i = 0..16 reads the object pointer table after tick_ms (0x0CE49F58[i + 1]), follows +0x14 to a state word and compares it, and an id byte (0x0CE49CBC), with the values in 0x0CE49C74; returns the bitmask of entries that differ. idleTASK (0x0C0B8EA2) calls it in a loop until it is non-zero, which is why most interrupts land at 0x0C0B8EFA and why it dominates loads from on-chip pool 2 [static + emu]. Empty slots make it load @(0x14, NULL): tens of millions of cached reads of flash 0x00000014 while idle (40M in a 100 s headless boot), harmless. Its loop is the CPU headroom gauge: under -icount (cache-model profiles, all-mods build 0.13) it is 66% of executed instructions in the boot to NO DISC, 91% during USB FLAC play (the FLAC decoder in the payload is about 3.4% of instructions) and 95% during USB WAV play with loops and hot cues [emu].
1 ms tick: increments 0x0CE49F54, then calls the power/standby part 0x0C0EF8C8 through pool 0x0C0B9310 (loaded at 0x0C0B92EA).
Pool word -> power_tick_1ms, loaded at 0x0C0B92EA. Mod payload_demo redirects it.

Finalizes DB menu results. Count is u16 at +2, primary sort mode is u8 at +4, and the u16 row index pointer is at +0x2C. A nonzero primary sort mode builds the index with the stock comparator. The finalizer then releases its sort workspace.

Finalizes the left buffer immediately before publishing it to the destination menu cache, shared by local menu requests. The browse mod writes the sorted cursor order into the index and skips the second title sort.
Reads WAV PCM data from a USB audio file (the flac mod redirects pool 0x0C0585F4).

USB playback decode step: usb_decoder_read(0x2DFE0000, &n), memset(0x2DFE0000, 0, n*4) to pad a short block, then pcm_rate_copy(0x2DFE0000 + skip*2, ...) into the PCM sector ring. 0x2DFE0000 is the uncached mirror of usb_pcm_decode_buf (0x0DFE0000); nothing touches it through the cached address, so no cache maintenance is needed. Used extent: WAV 0x0DFE0000-0x0DFE09FF, MP3 0x0DFE0000-0x0DFE11FF.
anlz_add_cue(db, track key, rec, hot): adds a memory cue (hot = 0, from memory_cue_add) or hot cue (hot = 1, via 0x0C0C166C) to the ANLZ file and writes it (0x0C0C17E6 -> 0x0C0C5960 -> 0x0C0C5EEC).
Fills hot-cue slot ctx + 0xF58 + n*0x38 (n = 1..3, tag PCPT, status 1) from the record, sets the PCOB count/length, then writes the section through pool 0x0C0C195C (0x0C0C5960).
Pool word -> anlz_write_section, read only at 0x0C0C17CE. Mod hot_cues (hot_cues_anlz) redirects it.
Reads rekordbox ANLZ PWAV (400 bytes -> 800-byte height/whiteness pairs at out+0) and PWV2 (100-byte overview at out+800) into the 900-byte waveform buffer (0x0CE65862).

Finds the ANLZ file of a track under <drive>:/PIONEER (or /.PIONEER)/USBANLZ/... and, when none matches and param_3 != 0, creates /ANLZ%04X.DAT with mode "w+" (pool 0x0C0C4004) and writes its header: the deck creates analysis files on the stick [static].

usb_anlz_mount(ctx, arg): USB ANLZ manager set-up of a newly mounted stick. Builds <drive>:/PIONEER (or /.PIONEER)/USBANLZ, opens /PIONEER/USBANLZ/USBMNG.DAT ("r+", created "w+" when missing) and indexes the P%03X folders. ctx+0xC is the drive record (first halfword = drive letter, "C" for USB), as anlz_find_or_create passes it to file_open_drive. Called through pool 0x0C0C11E8, read only at 0x0C0C1010 in FUN_0C0C0F88 (outside the boot-critical closure); quant_loops/waveform redirect it to c850_ui_usb_mount, which then reads the mod settings file /PIONEER/MODSET.DAT [static + emu].
anlz_write_section(file, ctx, 3, buf): rewrites the ANLZ file from the hot-cue tag on (pool 0x0C0C195C, read only at 0x0C0C17CE).

Template of the RTOS ISR wrapper. Pool-2 objects (0xFFF86638+) hold a copy of these bytes followed by the handler pointers, one per registered interrupt (e.g. at 0xFFF866E0, 0xFFF87BAC, 0xFFF8DC90, 0xFFF8DE9C), and the on-chip vector table at 0xFFF80000 (VBR) points at the copies [emu: on-chip RAM dump].
Writes INTC IPR08 (0xFFFE0C04) with CMI0 priority 7 in bits 7:4. IPR08 read as 0x6070 during stock USB playback. CMI0 vector 142 ties IRQ7 vector 71 at priority 7.
RTOS: sleep the calling task with a timeout.
RTOS: set event flag bits (audio_send_cmd sets flag 2 after queueing).
RTOS: wait on event flag (flag, pattern, mode, ..., timeout). DjControlTask waits on flag 2; playertask's loop waits at 0x0C0ED1B0 (pool 0x0C0ED244).
RTOS: send to mailbox (audio_send_cmd queues on mailbox 2).
RTOS polling receive from mailbox. DjControlTask uses mailbox 2 for audio commands.
Initialize RTOS kernel objects using SDRAM pool 1 at 0x0CEEFA20 and on-chip RAM pool 2 at 0xFFF86638.
RTOS: wait for a free message block; the only place audio_send_cmd can block, before it queues.
Returns USB INTSTS0.VBSTS (0xFFFC1C40 bit 7) once three reads one delay_flash_rd32x200(1) apart agree.
Base tempo outside 60.0..199.9 (999.0 with bpm999, constant at 0x0C0D1C80) stores 130.0 in the sync field.
Computes locked pitch (master_tenths*10000/base_tenths - 10000) into 0x0CE649BC and sets catch-up direction 0x0CE649BE. Stock clamps to +-0x640 (+-16%); mods/bpm_lock widens to +-0x2710 (+-100%).

CDJ-350 BPM Lock command dispatcher (cmds 0..9): 0=toggle lock, 1=enter/refresh Master BPM edit, 2=fader catch-up (from tempo_fader_to_pitch), 3/5/8=exit edit, 4=rotary adjust Master BPM, 6=recalc, 7=unlock, 9=get effective pitch (used by player_keys_latch_prev).
cue_select_from_list(src, dir): picks the next/previous memory cue or loop and fills the 0x24-byte jump record 0x0CE65C0C and the cue frame 0x0CE6D158.
memory_cue_add(src, 1): USB branch builds the 0x24 record from the loop/cue records and calls 0x0C0C1442 (rec, 0) to add it to the ANLZ file, then inserts it into the runtime list 0x0CE649D4.
cue_call_prev_next(next): CALL< (0) / CALL> (1). The USB branches call cue_select_from_list through pools 0x0C0D41BC (read at 0x0C0D3F5C) and 0x0C0D3CC8 (read at 0x0C0D3B94), chosen by 0x0CE6D254.
Pool word -> cue_select_from_list, read only at 0x0C0D3B94. Mod hot_cues (hot_cues_select2) redirects it.
MEMORY button: calls memory_cue_add on USB.
Pool word -> cue_select_from_list, read only at 0x0C0D3F5C. Mod hot_cues (hot_cues_select) redirects it.
Maps averaged 16-bit PCM amplitude to 1..15 waveform height using a 2 dB/step logarithmic threshold table (0x0517..0x50C3).
Shows a popup on the dot-matrix display by message id (e.g. 0x1F, 0x32B, 0x312, 0x311, 0x314).
Compute the DSP target speed from the fader, range, jog bend and VINYL ramp state. Updates 0x0CE6C940 and the HOLD flag at 0x0CE6C938.

Unpack panel button state using the tables at 0x0C194EA4 and 0x0C194FD8. Panel RX 0x01 carries rotary, pitch and jog words with checksum at byte 15. RX 0x02 carries button banks and the VINYL pot with checksum at byte 12.
Format and send an audio command packet via RTOS mailbox 2.
Dispatches the key handlers by player state. State 4 (USB loop playing) tail-jumps through pool 0x0C0D7B98 (read only at 0x0C0D79A6) to keys_state4_looping.
Pool word -> keys_state4_looping, read only by the tail jump at 0x0C0D79A6. Mods loop_resize and quant_loops share one redirect to the payload's c850_loop_tick.
Handles TEMPO range, MASTER TEMPO and TIME MODE/AUTO CUE button actions. Changing range or MT forces a speed/flag refresh even when the fader is unchanged.
Hook span 0x0C0D8DC2..0x0C0D8DCE (TEMPO range step). Mod tempo_wide steps 16% -> WIDE on USB.

TEMPO range step. r0 = *0x0CE6D25A (source, 1 = USB), r6 = *0x0CE6D0E1 (1=+-6 2=+-10 3=+-16 4=WIDE). USB: 1->2 2->3 3->1 4->3 (no WIDE); else (CD): 1->2 2->3 3->4 4->1. Next range r4 -> FUN at pool 0x0C0D8FA8. tempo_wide hooks 0x0C0D8DC2 and clears r0 so USB takes the CD table.
Toggle elapsed/remaining time at 0x0CE6D0DD. The REMAIN flag travels in status 0x02 byte 13 bit 0.
Toggle the auto-cue latch on a long TIME MODE press. Status 0x02 byte 12 bit 0 carries A.CUE.
Pool word -> memory_button, read only at 0x0C0D9664. Mod loop_resize redirects it.
Pool word -> cue_call_prev_next, read at 0x0C0D98AC (CALL>) and 0x0C0D98EA (CALL<). Mod loop_resize redirects it.

Tempo fader to pitch: from the fader sample 0x0CE6CA48 against the centre 0x0CE6CA4A writes the pitch word 0x0CE6CA50 (s16, 1/100 %, clamped to the range; WIDE flag 0x0CE6CA4C selects x50) and the whole pitched BPM 0x0C9D23F0 = round(round(base/10) * (10000+pitch)/10000).
Player tick processing jog motion for pitch bend and VINYL scratch velocity.
PLAY/PAUSE button handler. For USB the normal load-completion path starts playback. A subsequent PLAY press pauses/brakes, according to jog mode and player state.
Pool word -> pcm_next_feed_sector, read only at 0x0C0DF95E (LOOP IN). Mod quant_loops (quant_loops_loop_in) redirects it.
Pool word -> audio_send_cmd, read by the LOOP OUT code (and its CD branch). Mod quant_loops (quant_loops_loop_out) redirects it.
Pool word -> audio_send_cmd, read only by the LOOP OUT code. Mod quant_loops (quant_loops_loop_out2) redirects it.
Key handler for state 4 (a USB loop is playing), once per player cycle.
Copies the held key words K0..K2 (0x0CE6CA08..) to their _prev copies (0x0CE6CA22..) once per player cycle.

beat_loop_out_from_bpm(beats, &bpm, tracklen): bpm = round(base tempo 0x0C9D23EC / 10) (0 -> 130); 0x0CE6CA90 = D1C0 + 36000/bpm (8-beat limit); D1C0 += beats*4500 / (bpm * (D154*15 + 1)), clamped to tracklen-1, so D1C0 (0x0CE6D1C0) becomes the out frame. Returns 1 only when enough audio is buffered past the out point.

auto_beat_loop_set(beats 1/2/4/8): stores beats in 0x0C1E1088. With no loop active (0x0CE6D0ED == 0) sets D1C0 (0x0CE6D1C0) to the current frame, runs beat_loop_out_from_bpm and sends audio cmd 6 with the out frame. The other audio_send_cmd loads in it are the resize sends (flag 1).
Pool word -> audio_send_cmd, read only in auto_beat_loop_set (cued path, 0x0C0E5CC8). Mod quant_loops (quant_loops_auto_send2) redirects it.
Pool word -> track_length_slot, read only at 0x0C0E5C0E in auto_beat_loop_set's new-loop path. Mod quant_loops redirects it.
Pool word -> audio_send_cmd, read only in auto_beat_loop_set (play path, 0x0C0E5D90). Mod quant_loops (quant_loops_auto_send) redirects it.
Pool word -> pcm_next_feed_sector, read only at 0x0C0E5DAA, right after the cmd 6 sends. Mod quant_loops (quant_loops_auto_keep) redirects it.

Rotary scroll in UTILITY level 2. Pool 0x0C0E797C calls utility_scroll_item with 0=CCW, 1=CW and the detent count. Stock clamps the item at 0..6. waveform and quant_loops redirect it to the shared c850_ui_utility_scroll, which continues the list after VERSION No. with the mod items (WAVE PLAYHEAD, then QUANTIZE DRIFT) as items 7, 8, ...

INFO screen rotary scroll handler (nav_view_selector == 0, not BPM Lock edit): increments/decrements info_cursor (0x0CE6D1E4) based on direction byte at sp+0x1c (0=CCW, 1=CW). Hooked by mods/waveform (waveform_rotary_hook) to zoom out/in at cursor 0.

Encoder press in the main UTILITY list. Pool 0x0C0E7F10 calls utility_set_menu_level(3, item). waveform and quant_loops redirect it to the shared c850_ui_utility_select: a press on a mod item (7, 8, ...) switches its value in place (WAVE PLAYHEAD: Left 1/3/Center/Left, flags 0x0C9DA25E bit 0x04 and 0x0C9DA25D bit 0x01; QUANTIZE DRIFT ON/OFF: 0x0C9DA25D bit 0x02); other items go to stock utility_set_menu_level.
USB load-completion state selection. The normal path selects playing state 3 and sends audio command (1, 1). The audio task starts streaming after 75 buffered sectors.

Player state tick, every player cycle (bsr at 0x0C0ED274). Calls 0x0C0EB388 first through pool 0x0C0EC838 (read only at 0x0C0EC73E). With the UI lock 0x0CE6D151 set it saves K0..K2 to 0x0CE6CA14 and masks them.
Pool word -> 0x0C0EB388, read only at 0x0C0EC73E (first call of player_state_tick). Mod hot_cues (hot_cues_tick) redirects it.

Builds the held key words K0/K1/K2 (0x0CE6CA08..) from the accepted panel keys. Called only by the bsr at 0x0C0ED1FA in the playertask loop when the new-keys flag 0x0CE6D132 is set. Calls the key filter through pool 0x0C0ED038 (read at 0x0C0ECEFC) right after K0..K2 are built.
Copy the received SCIF1 0x01 fader position and center reference (wire bytes 5..8, big-endian) into 0x0CE6CA48 and 0x0CE6CA4A.
Pool word -> 0x0C0DD492, the key filter point, read only at 0x0C0ECEFC after K0..K2 are built. Mods hot_cues and quant_loops redirect it to the payload's c850_ui_keys chain.

playertask entry (priority 2): the key loop. Calls panel_keys_to_internal_words (0x0C0ED1FA), player_state_tick (0x0C0ED274) and the key handlers, and waits on an event flag at 0x0C0ED1B0 (pool 0x0C0ED244).
Pool word -> wai_flg, read only at 0x0C0ED1B0 in the playertask loop. Mod hot_cues (hot_cues_leds) redirects it.
Requests an asynchronous USB browse update (r4 = 1 for the browser). The stock BROWSE action calls this from the player task.

Sets S[0x15] (TX 0x02 byte 8): bit 0 = arg bit 0 (auto-standby request, power_state_tick 0x0C0EFAAE), bit 2 = arg bit 2 (firmware-update mode: set by the RELOOP-held boot path 0x0C0ED01C, cleared by the updater at 0x0C08EBD2).
Idle auto-standby countdown: counts whole seconds in 0x0C1E10AE and asks for standby at the limit from table 0x0C18CCDC, indexed by (UTILITY byte 0x0C9DA23E >> 4) & 7.
Power/standby part of the 1 ms tick (from tick_1ms through pool 0x0C0B9310). Calls auto_standby_seconds.
Power/standby state machine, called at 0x0C0EE644.

pcm_ring_write(src, frames): copies stereo frames into the PCM ring at pcm_ring_or_update_buffer: 0x961 slots of 0x24C frames (0x930 bytes, one CD-DA sector of PCM each), advancing the slot index and wrapping after slot 0x960. The third copy of every PCM byte in USB playback. Called from 0x0C0C02D4 [static + emu].

audio_build_loop_in_record(sector): builds the loop-in record 0x0C7F6498.. (frame, MSF, ring sector) from the s16 sector 0x0C7F6468 (writer 0x0C0F022A). Called by 0x0C009DB4 for audio cmd 6 and cmd 7/2. A sector ahead of the playhead works for cmd 6: the feeder plays on to it, then loops in..out (BEAT 4 at frame 301 with the sector of 308: wrap 447 -> 308) [emu].

Reader timeout expiry: reached when audio_read_timeout 0x0C7F6648 counts down to 0 (decrement 0x0C0F1260) or from state 6 (0x0C0F124C); reports to the audio task with FUN_0C009310(8, .., 2, -0x6F) [static]. Not reached in search/jog runs (stock WAV, flac mod, icount shift 2-5): the countdown is only armed by the cue prefill (0x0C0F533E) [emu].

USB cue prefill (CALL of a memory cue, a hot_cues jump; state 6 with 0x0CE6D26A = 0xFF): mov #100,r14; shll2 r14 = 400 sectors (5.33 s of audio), requested at 0x0C0F534E as FUN_0C008C8A(4, *0x0C7F6494, .., 0x0C7F673E, 400, 120, ..): fill ring slots from 120. r14 + 100 = 500 goes to the reader timeout 0x0C7F6648 (0x0C0F535A..0x0C0F5362), which the reader counts down (0x0C0F1258). Emulator (WAV stick, stock): write index 120 -> 520, ready 100 ms of guest time after the CALL. On a deck, reading and decoding these 5.33 s is the several-second CALL/hot-cue delay. Inside the boot-critical closure (0x0C0F494C..0x0C0F63F0), so no mod changes it [static + emu].

Cue ready: when the prefill read is done (0x0C7F663D != 0, 0x0C7F656E == 0) this branch rebuilds the loop-in record, clears 0x0C7F6640 and calls FUN_0C009272(7, 0, 0, 5, ..) and FUN_0C009310(5, 1, 32, ..), which sets 0x0C7F6627 = 5 (from 0x15 while prefilling); playertask then sets 0x0CE6D26A = 5 (0x0C0EDA6C) and the state-6 handler takes PLAY [emu: gdb write watches].

USB playback state handler and refill scheduler. USB state at 0x0CE6D25F includes browse 0x0A, load 2, play 3, pause 4 and brake/pause 5. Refills the circular PCM ring while fill is below 500 sectors.

pcm_rate_init(rate): zeroes a 12-byte buffer and a counter, stores rate in pcm_sample_rate (0x0CE6DBAC), then calls 0x0C0F96A8(rate). usb_decode_fill (0x0C0BF6BA) calls it at 0x0C0BF748 with sample_rate_table[record +0x3A2 bits 5-8] before the decode loop [static].

pcm_rate_copy(src, dst, ?, samples, &frames_out): if pcm_sample_rate (0x0CE6DBAC) is 44100, memcpy samples * 2 bytes from src (wav_decode_block's uncached buffer) to dst and report samples / 2 frames; otherwise resamples block by block through pcm_resample_cubic (0x0C0F97B8), keeping the remainder in a carry buffer. Called from 0x0C0BF6BA [static + emu].

pcm_resample_cubic(src, dst, channels, in_frames, out_frames): converts 16-bit frames to out_frames with a 4-point cubic interpolator, 11-bit fractional position, integer only, clipped to 16 bits; stereo when channels == 2. Copies the last 3 input frames (12 bytes) ahead of src for the next call. Called only from pcm_rate_copy (0x0C0F9644) for rates other than 44100 [static].
Eight-bit end-around-carry checksum. MAIN TX and panel RX 0x01 sum bytes 0..14 into byte 15. Panel RX 0x02 sums bytes 0..11 into byte 12.
Set up SCIF1 at 0xFFFE8800 as clock-synchronous slave. IC1007 is clock master. MAIN_XBUSY is PC14 and PNL_XBUSY is PE9/IRQ5.
On PNL_XBUSY rising edge, IRQ5 vector 69 starts the transaction and preloads its first 16-byte MAIN TX frame.
SCIF1 TXI1 vector 199 services further 16-byte frames in the same PNL_XBUSY window until MAIN clears TIE.

Clears the CD sector ring: memset(0x2DF79F50, 0, 0x660B0) through the uncached mirror, 151 slots of 0xAD0 ending exactly at 0x0DFE0000 (the size is a movi20 immediate, so no literal shows it). Runs at boot (104,492 longword stores). Not a function in a fresh import; created by the annotation script.

Reads ring slot r4 of the CD sector ring through the uncached mirror (0x2DF79F50 + slot * 0xAD0), checks its header and copies 8 bytes from slot+0x10 or +0x18 to 0x0CEE3110. Called per slot from the loop at 0x0C0FB6A2. [static; CD playback is not emulated]

ocache_purge_range(r4 = start, r5 = length): for each 16-byte line stores start & 0x1FFFF800 (tag, U = V = 0) to 0xF0800008 + (start & 0x7F0), stepping both by 16 (the entry wraps into the don't-care address bits). Associative operand-cache address-array writes: a dirty line is written back, then dropped (SH7263 manual 8.4.3). Runs from cached SDRAM, unlike the boot's copy in on-chip RAM; MAIN's only cache maintenance (382k array writes in a USB play run) [static + emu].
Maps INFO text words 0x0526 and 0x0626 to panel bytes 0x04 (filled star) and 0x05 (open star) [static, words confirmed in QEMU].
MAIN-side transfer on the CD servo bus to IC201 (TC94A15FG). PE6 is SRVCCE, PE8 is SRVBCLK and PE12..15 are SRVBUS0..3.
Bring up the CD servo on its Port E bus. PE7 is SRVRST.

Bus delay: r4 dummy byte reads of flash 0x20000000 through the uncached mirror (the decompiler drops the dead load). Called by servo_transfer and the CD servo bit-bang routines 0x0C0FC886-0x0C0FD3C0; ~100k uncached reads per boot.
USBI vector 140. Dispatches via the USB mode word at 0x0CEE505C. Mode 1 invokes the host path at 0x0C018F44.
usbTask entry from the task descriptor at 0x0C1ACBC4. The board uses one USB controller with PB10 selecting USB-A host (high) or USB-B PC device (low).
Poll USB_CDETFLG on PE10 (high normal, low overcurrent) and update the overcurrent flag at 0x0C1E1271.

usb_file_open(path16, mode): fopen of the media file system. The drive letter (lower-cased) picks the device entry (table stride 0xC, type 3 = USB, takes the FS semaphore around the call; type 4 = other). Returns a file handle or 0. "w"/"w+" create or truncate [static + emu].
Closes a USB file (the flac mod redirects pool 0x0C058150).
Size of a USB file (the flac mod redirects pools 0x0C057F1C and 0x0C05814C).
wcscpy16(dst, src): copies a 0-terminated 16-bit string (paths of the file layer are 16-bit characters; file_open_drive copies its path argument with it, so the path must already be 16-bit) [static].

C library memcpy(dst r4, src r5, n r6); word-aligned copies go to memcpy_aligned (0x0C11066C). The emulator's CDJ_NATIVE_COPY hook recognises it by its first opcode 0xE218. During USB WAV playback three callers move ~87% of its bytes: wav_decode_block, pcm_rate_copy and pcm_ring_write [static + emu: call trace].

Inner loop of memcpy: 32 bytes per iteration in eight longword loads and stores (r9-r14 saved), byte tail. The function the cache model's USB-play profile charges most line fills to, as memcpy runs over large PCM buffers; ~1.4M of its reads and writes go through the uncached SDRAM mirror (wav_decode_block's buffer) [static + emu].
memcpy's word-aligned path: one longword, then 8-byte pairs until the length is a multiple of 32, then memcpy_block32 (0x0C1105D4), or a byte tail for under 4 bytes [static].

C library memset(dst r4, byte r5, n r6), filling backwards from the end in 16-byte longword blocks. 1031 references; most bytes come from large clears (alloc_zeroed, table resets). On the write-allocate operand cache every missed line is first read from SDRAM: 609k write misses in a USB play run. The emulator's CDJ_NATIVE_COPY hook recognises it by its first opcode 0x2FE6 [static + emu].

MP3 output stage: converts one granule (576 stereo frames, or 288 mono) from float to clipped 16-bit pairs packed in longwords and stores them through the uncached mirror into usb_pcm_decode_buf (0x2DFE0000). 1.27M uncached stores in a short MP3 run.
The hottest routine of the MP3 decoder core (0x0C13EC04..0x0C141FD8): 43M accesses to the on-chip MP3 work buffers in a 30 s USB MP3 run [emu].

sample_rate_table: 12 u32 rates indexed by record +0x3A2 bits 5-8: 96000, 88200, 64000, 48000, 44100, 32000, 24000, 22050, 16000, 12000, 11025, 8000 (the MPEG-4 sampling-frequency index order). Read by usb_decode_fill (0x0C0BF6E4) for pcm_rate_init, and by 0x0C0005F4, 0x0C0584B4, 0x0C08E460, 0x0C08F590, 0x0C08F64A, 0x0C08F7AA, 0x0C08F904, 0x0C0903D0 [static].

USB playback sub-state (record 0x0C7F6620 + 5) switched on by player_tick_usb_playback: 0x10-0x17 when +6 is 0, 0x20-0x2B when +6 is 1, 0x30-0x32 when +6 is 2 [static]. Observed [emu]: 0x30 at load, 0x10 while playing, 0x11/0x12 briefly when a refill is scheduled, and 0x12 during SEARCH underruns in the original FLAC prototype.

Observed [emu]: PCM ring sectors buffered ahead of playback. Drops to 0 when the ring restarts (track load, SEARCH press, SEARCH release), rises as the audio task fills, falls by 75/s while no reads run; stock WAV holds ~900-1240.
Observed [emu]: played sectors still held in the ring behind playback. Reset on a ring restart, climbs by 75/s during playback and stops at 1001.
u16 S+0xC, sent as TX 0x01 bytes 13..14. No store in MAIN; 0 in all captures (unused).
S[0x18], TX 0x02 byte 11: bits 1:0 pitch sign, bit 2 FL BROWSE legend, bit 3 FL TAG LIST legend, bit 4 FL MEMORY legend, bit 7 FL MT legend; bits 5, 6 unused.
S[0x19], TX 0x02 byte 12: bit 0 FL A.CUE legend, bit 3 FL CUE legend, bits 5:4 pitch decimals, bit 6 BPM legend group (with S[0x1B] bit 3), bit 7 FL INFO legend; bits 1, 2 unused.
TX 0x80 byte 11: bits 0..4 header status code (display_stage_header_status), bits 5..7 per-row flags for rows 1..3 (display_set_row_flag).
